title: pricing-packaging-back-of-envelope-notes-sam-2026-03-04
content:
Quick back-of-envelope notes for pricing / packaging options. Mostly thinking aloud.

Context / goals:
- Want simple self-serve pricing that's PLG-friendly but also clear upgrade paths to Dedicated/Private.
- Need to make sure hosted unit economics (per-token) are healthy vs Dedicated and Private sales motions.
- Provide transparent per-token pricing for customers and have obvious levers (batching, caching, quantization) for cost control.

Assumptions (rough, to revise):
- GPU cost (amortized infra + network + infra ops) ranges a lot by model: assume H100-style/managed infra cost to us = $3/hr (low) to $12/hr (high) per GPU depending on utilization/commit.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) depends on model size and optimizations. Quick estimates: small models (7-13B): 200-1,000 tok/s; medium (13-34B): 80-400 tok/s; large (70B+): 20-120 tok/s.
- Use tokens/hr = tok/s * 3600.

Cost per million tokens (GPU-only simplified) calculations:
- Example A: 13B model, 300 tok/s -> 1,080,000 tok/hr. If GPU cost = $6/hr -> cost per million tokens ~= $5.6. (calc: 6 / 1.08)
- Example B: 70B model, 60 tok/s -> 216,000 tok/hr. GPU cost = $8/hr -> cost per million tokens ~= $37.0.
- Example C: 7B model, 800 tok/s -> 2,880,000 tok/hr. GPU cost = $3/hr -> cost per million tokens ~= $1.04.

Notes on non-GPU costs to include later: storage (model weights), S3 egress, network, orchestration overhead, customer support, SRE ops, amortized infra management. Add ~20-40% on top of GPU-only to get total cost (very rough).

So approximate TOTAL cost per million tokens (with overhead multiplier):
- 7B: $1.3 - $1.8 per M
- 13B: $6.5 - $8.0 per M
- 70B+: $44 - $55 per M

Pricing sketch (hosted API) - list price ideas: aim for 3x-8x gross margin depending on segment and model:
- Free / dev: 100k tokens/month free (low friction).
- Hobby: $10/month -> 1M tokens included (equivalent price = $10 per M). Target model family: 7B.
- Startup: $100/month -> 12M tokens included ($8.3 per M). Good for small integrations and prototyping; use 13B family by default.
- Business: $1,000/month -> 150M tokens included ($6.6 per M). Bulk discounts, priority, SLA.
- Enterprise: custom pricing / committed spend, or Dedicated offering; reserve GPUs/throughput.

These suggested list prices are intentionally above the rough TOTAL cost to leave room for discounts, credits, sustained usage, and enterprise margins. Example mapping: Hobby -> mostly 7B; Startup -> 13B standard; Business -> 13B/70B mixed via routing; Enterprise -> 70B+ or private models.

Pay-as-you-go (metered) option:
- Offer per-1k token rates for on-demand: e.g., 13B @ $0.009 per 1k (=$9 per M), 70B @ $0.045 per 1k (=$45 per M). These map to ~1.1x-1.5x the list-included per-M price for small plans.

Dedicated / Reserved capacity:
- Price per GPU-hour (committed): include discounted rate for committed 1/3/12 month contracts. Example: H100-equivalent dedicated price = $6/hr (committed) vs hosted variable cost = $8-12/hr. Add management fee (20-30%) and base platform fee.
- Offer "Dedicated Lite": mid-tier where customers reserve fractional capacity or tail-latency SLA but share machines with soft isolation.

Unit economics examples for a SaaS app (example customer):
- App uses 1M tokens/day -> 30M tokens/month. If routed to 13B model and list price is $9/M -> revenue = $270/month. Cost (total per-M ~ $7) -> cost = $210 -> gross margin = 22%. Hit or miss depending on support and SRE costs. Need to move heavy users to committed pricing or Dedicated.

Behavioral levers to improve unit economics (what we can expose to customers + platform ops):
- Default to smaller model family for >X% of requests unless customer pins model. (auto model scaling)
- Smart routing: latency-sensitive -> fall back to proximate region/duplicate cheaper model.
- Adaptive sampling: reduce max tokens by default for cheaper tiers, encourage summarization/brevity.
- Caching & prefix caching: 1-2% of tokens saved can be meaningful at scale.
- Batching and multiplexing: increase effective tokens/s served per GPU at cost of some latency.
- Quantization-aware model variants: 4-bit variants reduce GPU cost by 30-50%.

Tier features (sketch):
- Free: 100k tokens/mo, community support, 1 req/sec rate limit
- Hobby ($10/mo): 1M tokens, model pool: 7B quantized, no SLA, basic dashboard
- Startup ($100/mo): 12M tokens, 13B quantized, moderate rate limits, trial Dedicated credits, priority queueing
- Business ($1k/mo): 150M tokens, 13B/70B mixed, SLA 99.9, tracing + per-route dashboards, alerting, rollout controls
- Enterprise: custom, Dedicated/private option, advanced compliance, longer retention, white-glove onboarding

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need better telemetry on actual tokens/sec per model under our runtime (real experiments). TODO: run synthetic benchmarks at common batch sizes and sequence lengths and capture 7/13/70B throughput.
- Validate GPU amortized cost by region and committed discount assumptions with infra finance.
- Model mapping: when do we route to small vs large model? Build heuristic based on prompt length + expected completion length + quality metrics.
- Pricing psychology: round numbers, anchor to $/M tokens, but also present monthly bundles. Test A/B for $9 vs $12 per M.
- Decide on free tier size vs abuse risk. 100k seems fine but open to reduce.
- Define upgrade path from hosted payg to Dedicated reservation credits.

Random notes:
- We should publish a simple per-M table in docs with "typical model family costs" to help customers choose.
- Consider a Builder credit for startups that cross X usage in first 90 days.

End of scratchpad. Will convert to a more formal pricing doc once we have measured throughput numbers and finance-backed GPU cost inputs.

Questions for next sync:
- Infra finance: real blended GPU/hr by region at different commit levels?
- Bench team: run throughput matrix for 7/13/70B across batch sizes and sequence lengths (p50, p95).
- Sales/CS: what are common token volumes we see in early enterprise trials currently?
summary: Back-of-envelope unit-economics and tier ideas for hosted API: per-M token cost estimates by model family, suggested list prices and tier breakdowns, levers to improve margins, and action items for validation.
